title: Scheduler change triggered repeated kernel fallback and 99th-pct latency spike
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After deploying runtime-2.3.1 which included a scheduler tweak to favor throughput for GPU pools, we observed a 2x increase in 99th-percentile token latency on select production clusters (region: us-west-2) beginning 2026-03-09 03:14 UTC. Investigation shows repeated kernel fallbacks and JIT/compilation churn caused by an incorrect cache-key when the scheduler adjusted batch shapes. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, temporary mitigations, long-term action items, and owners.
timeline: 2026-03-09 03:14 UTC - Synthetic and customer telemetry: 99p token latency increases from ~120ms to ~260ms on serving-pool-gpu-03 (us-west-2). Error rates low; throughput slightly higher.
2026-03-09 03:18 UTC - Pager triggered for latency SLO breach; on-call alerted (Liam O'Connor).
2026-03-09 03:25 UTC - Initial rollback of scheduler policy to previous default (runtime-2.3.0 behavior) applied to a canary subset; latency improved but not fully back to baseline.
2026-03-09 04:05 UTC - Full rollback to scheduler behavior pre-2.3.1 completed; 95p/99p latency trending back toward baseline over 30-45 minutes.
2026-03-09 05:00 UTC - Post-incident triage started; responsible teams: serving-runtime, compilation, scheduler.

2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Reproduction in staging: running mixed sequence-length workload reproduces repeated kernel fallback and spike in per-token p99. Confirmed kernel cache key mismatch when batch shape altered by scheduler heuristics.

2026-03-11 14:30 UTC - Root cause hypothesis validated: scheduler-induced batch reshaping combined with an insufficiently discriminative kernel cache key caused the runtime to mark an existing compiled kernel as incompatible, triggering fallback to a safe path and subsequent recompilations under load.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Draft mitigation: tighten cache key and add guard to avoid recompilation during transient batch shape fluctuations. Tests in CI added and running.
root_cause: A scheduler policy change (throughput-favoring heuristics) altered the batch shape distribution at runtime. The kernel cache key used by the compilation module did not include the batch-sequence-length-vector in a stable way, so when the scheduler reordered or reshaped in-flight batches the runtime treated compatible kernels as mismatches. This caused repeated fallback to a slower generic kernel and triggered repeated JIT/compilation churn under production load, amplifying p99 latency.
mitigations: Immediate: Rolled back scheduler heuristics to pre-2.3.1 behavior across affected pools (completed 2026-03-09 04:05 UTC).
Short-term: Added runtime guard to skip recompilation if an existing compiled kernel differs only by non-critical batch metadata (hotfix branch runtime/hotfix/ENG-9427).
Monitoring: Instrumented kernel-selection miss metric (metric: runtime.kernel_cache.miss_reason) and added alert when miss_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m.
Customer comms: Notified affected customers with increased latency; offered follow-up with account SREs for Dedicated customers.
action_items: (Owner: Mateo Ruiz) Add batch-shape components to kernel cache key deterministically and publish change as runtime-2.3.2 candidate. ETA: 2026-03-18
(Owner: Priya Desai) Expand unit + integration tests to simulate scheduler-driven batch reshaping and assert no kernel cache churn under mixed sequence workloads. ETA: 2026-03-16

(Owner: Liam O'Connor) Harden scheduler rollout process: add canary traffic shaping and latency guard rails that auto-abort policy changes when 95p latency regresses by >15% in canary. ETA: 2026-03-22
(Owner: Engineering Tools) Add synthetic workload to perf-lab that exercises short/long sequence mixes (repo: infra/perf-recipes#24). ETA: 2026-03-19
(Owner: Aisha Patel) Execute post-deploy verification playbook and update runbook with kernel-cache-miss troubleshooting steps. ETA: 2026-03-15
(Owner: Observability) Create dashboard tile for runtime.kernel_cache.* metrics and link to Oncall runbook. ETA: 2026-03-14
monitoring_updates: New metrics created: runtime.kernel_cache.hit_rate, runtime.kernel_cache.miss_reason, runtime.kernel_recompile.rate
Alert rule: KERNEL_CACHE_MISS_HIGH fires when runtime.kernel_cache.miss_rate > 0.5% for 5m in any production pool
Added dashboard: Runtime -> Kernel Stability (showing p50/p95/p99 token latency vs kernel miss rate)

2026-03-10 14:45 - Mateo Ruiz: Preliminary fix for cache key submitted (PR 1891). Needs review from compilation team; concern about key size impacting lookup latency.

2026-03-11 09:07 - Priya Desai: Added integration test that runs a 30-minute mixed workload and asserts stable kernel cache hit rate > 99%. Found one flake related to padding normalization — pushing follow-up patch.

2026-03-11 16:30 - Simon Leung (Compilation): Reviewed PR; requested benchmark numbers for lookup latency and memory overhead. Also suggested adding a compacted fingerprint instead of raw vector in cache key.
2026-03-12 08:20 - Aisha Patel: Oncall playbook updated and verified end-to-end. Notifying ops to watch for KERNEL_CACHE_MISS_HIGH for next 72 hours post deploy.
